Abstract: Genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions.. Early diagnosis of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) and its precursors is still a challenge to overcome. So far, research on the genomic characterization of VSCC tumors has been limited. We retrospectively analyzed mutational data, histology, and clinical features of eight samples from six patients (including four HPV-negative VSCC patients with adjacent differentiated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN) tissues, one vulvar lichen sclerosus patient, and one vulvar acanthosis with altered differentiation-like patient). Targeted deep sequencing was performed on these samples with adjacent normal tissues as controls. Only one VSCC patient had moderately/poorly differentiated carcinoma, and neither TP53 nor PIK3CA mutations were identified in this case. Abstract: Invasive Lobular Carcinoma With Extracellular Mucin Production: First Whole Exome Sequencing of a Rare Histological Variant of Breast Carcinoma.. Invasive lobular carcinoma with extracellular mucin production (ILCEMP) is a rare histological variant of invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), with only about 40 cases described in the English literature. In the latest WHO classification of breast tumours, ILCEMP is described under the mucinous carcinoma section, noting that it is not certain whether these tumours represent a subtype of ILC or mucinous carcinoma. We performed whole-exome sequencing in seven ILCEMP primary tumors and two matched regional metastatic lymph nodes from seven patients. Samples were provided by six different European institutions. Most cases have been previously described histologically in two studies. data.text: PMID 42621186: "Identification of novel UBE2E3::PDE1A and CTC1::MEF2C fusion transcripts in acute myeloid leukemia." (Ther Adv Hematol, 2026). Abstract: Identification of novel. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a hematologic malignancy caused by the malignant proliferation and differentiation block of immature myeloid cells (blasts) in the bone marrow. The pathogenesis, diagnostic classification, treatment, and prognosis of AML are fundamentally linked to the accumulation of genetic variants, fusion gene formation, and chromosomal karyotype abnormalities. Using mRNA sequencing (next-generation sequencing, NGS), we identified and validated two novel fusion genes, UBE2E3::PDE1A and CTC1::MEF2C, in a case of AML-M2a. This patient also harbored six single nucleotide variants (SNV) (EP300, KRAS, NRAS, RAD21, TET2, and TP53) and complex karyotype (CK). The chromosomes exhibited extreme instability and high variability, with tumor cells containing multiple clones and showing continuous karyotype evolution as the disease progressed. claims.text: Clinical Interpretation for TP53 Variant rs28934578
The variant rs28934578 in the TP53 gene is classified as Likely Pathogenic (review status: reviewed by expert panel) by ClinVar.
This variant is a missense and coding sequence variant, which can potentially alter the function of the TP53 protein, a critical tumor suppressor gene.
TP53 mutations are strongly associated with various types of cancer, including but not limited to breast, ovarian, and colorectal cancers.

The variant rs28934578 has been implicated in the genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) and its precursor lesions, as evidenced by the recent study by [Genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8294754/).
The penetrance of TP53 mutations can vary widely, but they are generally associated with a high risk of developing cancer.

The expressivity of the variant rs28934578 is not well-documented, but given its classification as Likely Pathogenic, it is reasonable to assume that it could contribute to the development of cancer, particularly VSCC.
Given the potential pathogenicity of the TP53 variant rs28934578, individuals carrying this variant should be monitored closely for early signs of cancer.
Regular screening and surveillance for VSCC and other cancers associated with TP53 mutations are recommended.
Genetic counseling should be provided to discuss the implications of the variant and the potential risks to family members.
The evidence supporting the pathogenicity of rs28934578 is based on the ClinVar classification and recent research on VSCC.

The study by [Genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8294754/) provides direct evidence linking this variant to VSCC, although the sample size is small.
Additional studies with larger cohorts are needed to further validate the clinical significance of this variant.
The TP53 variant rs28934578 is classified as Likely Pathogenic and is associated with an increased risk of VSCC and other cancers.
Individuals with this variant should undergo regular surveillance and genetic counseling.
The evidence supporting this classification is based on ClinVar and recent research, but further validation is warranted.

data.title: Clinical Interpretation
data.content:
### Clinical Interpretation for TP53 Variant rs28934578

#### 1. Clinical Significance
The variant rs28934578 in the TP53 gene is classified as Likely Pathogenic (review status: reviewed by expert panel) by ClinVar. This variant is a missense and coding sequence variant, which can potentially alter the function of the TP53 protein, a critical tumor suppressor gene.

#### 2. Disease Associations
TP53 mutations are strongly associated with various types of cancer, including but not limited to breast, ovarian, and colorectal cancers. The variant rs28934578 has been implicated in the genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) and its precursor lesions, as evidenced by the recent study by [Genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8294754/).

#### 3. Penetrance & Expressivity
The penetrance of TP53 mutations can vary widely, but they are generally associated with a high risk of developing cancer. The expressivity of the variant rs28934578 is not well-documented, but given its classification as Likely Pathogenic, it is reasonable to assume that it could contribute to the development of cancer, particularly VSCC.

#### 4. Clinical Management
Given the potential pathogenicity of the TP53 variant rs28934578, individuals carrying this variant should be monitored closely for early signs of cancer. Regular screening and surveillance for VSCC and other cancers associated with TP53 mutations are recommended. Genetic counseling should be provided to discuss the implications of the variant and the potential risks to family members.

#### 5. Evidence Quality
The evidence supporting the pathogenicity of rs28934578 is based on the ClinVar classification and recent research on VSCC. The study by [Genomic signatures of HPV-independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma and its precursor lesions](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8294754/) provides direct evidence linking this variant to VSCC, although the sample size is small. Additional studies with larger cohorts are needed to further validate the clinical significance of this variant.

### Summary
The TP53 variant rs28934578 is classified as Likely Pathogenic and is associated with an increased risk of VSCC and other cancers. Individuals with this variant should undergo regular surveillance and genetic counseling. The evidence supporting this classification is based on ClinVar and recent research, but further validation is warranted.
